title: Unsafe Deserialization and Reviver Misuse
platform_conditions: ECMAScript 2020 semantics in Node.js runtime; XML entity behavior depends on the parser in use
security_mechanism: Historically, JavaScript 'deserialization' meant evaluating the payload -- new Function('return ' + text) or eval -- which executes embedded code verbatim. JSON.parse itself never executes code, but its reviver argument is called for every key with attacker-chosen key/value pairs, so a reviver that dispatches on key names into constructors or setters turns the payload into a constructor/property-assignment gadget chain. Server-side XML parsers invoked with entity processing enabled resolve external entities, giving file read and SSRF with the payload alone.

source_sink_clues.source: Request bodies, stored blobs, cross-service messages, and XML/config documents received from peers or uploads.
source_sink_clues.sink: new Function / eval used to reconstruct objects from text; JSON.parse with a reviver that assigns or constructs from attacker keys; XML parsers with entity expansion enabled

tracking_guards: Check data-only payloads are read with plain JSON.parse and a schema validator rather than evaluation; check the reviver is a constant function that never calls constructors or writes to objects by attacker-supplied key; check XML parsing disables DTD/entity resolution.
not_candidate_when: The payload is parsed with JSON.parse and validated against a schema before use, the reviver only filters/prunes known keys with fixed logic, or the XML producer is a trusted internal service that never emits DTDs.
public_references: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/611.html
